claim:
For the Bravyi–Kitaev H-type 15-to-1 magic-state distillation map on twirled independent inputs
\[
\rho_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)|H\rangle\langle H|+\epsilon|-H\rangle\langle-H|,
\qquad 0\le \epsilon\le \frac12,
\]
the nontrivial fixed-point threshold is exactly
\[
\epsilon_*=\frac12\left(1-\sqrt{\frac{z_*-\sqrt{z_*^2-4}}{2}}\right)
=0.141480292656167238344579330466\ldots,
\]
where \(z_*\) is the unique real root in \((2,3)\) of
\[
z^3+z^2-2z-16=0.
\]
Equivalently, with \(r_*=1-2\epsilon_*\) and \(y_*=r_*^2\), \(y_*\in(0,1)\) is the unique physical nonunit root of
\[
y^7-15y^4+15y^3-1=0.
\]
The only fixed points on \([0,1/2]\) are \(0,\epsilon_*,1/2\). Every initial \(0<\epsilon<\epsilon_*\) yields a strictly decreasing iteration converging to \(0\), while every \(\epsilon_*<\epsilon<1/2\) yields a strictly increasing iteration converging to \(1/2\). Thus the source's numerically quoted \(0.141\) threshold admits an exact algebraic description and complete basin classification for this specific 15-to-1 protocol. This is not a claim about the globally best H-state distillation threshold, which later protocols improve.

scientific_limitations: The threshold and basin are for the specific Bravyi–Kitaev H-type 15-to-1 recurrence after H-twirling, not for globally optimal magic-state distillation.
The analysis assumes independent identically distributed input states and ideal Clifford operations/postselection as in the source model.
Later H-state protocols have larger distillation regions, so an input above this threshold can still be distillable by another routine.
title: Exact algebraic threshold and global basin for the Bravyi–Kitaev H-state 15-to-1 map
